Instructions Provide your responses to the following questions in both R and Python. Follow the guidelines @ assign3_guidelines for more direction. Also, make sure to use the supporting scripts @ 06_explore_data.

Visualizations

Question #1: Create a boxplot.

#Importing the Data:
library(datasets)
data("iris")
data = iris 

#Importing the libraries necessary:
library(caret)
## Loading required package: lattice
## Loading required package: ggplot2
library(AppliedPredictiveModeling)

#Making the Box Plot:
featurePlot(x = data[, 1:4], 
            y = data$Species, 
            plot = "box", 
            ## Pass in options to bwplot() 
            scales = list(y = list(relation="free"),
                          x = list(rot = 90)),  
            layout = c(4,1 ), 
            auto.key = list(columns = 2))

Question #2: Create a barplot.

#Importing the libraries:
library(ggplot2)

#Importing the Data:
data('iris')
data = iris 

#Creating the Bar plot:
p = ggplot(data, aes(Species, Sepal.Length)) +
  stat_summary(fun.y = mean,
               geom = "bar",
               fill = "White", 
               color = "Black") + 
  stat_summary(fun.data = mean_cl_normal, 
               geom = "errorbar", 
               position = position_dodge(width = 0.90), 
               width = 0.2) + 
  xlab('Iris Flower Type')+
  ylab('Measurements')
## Warning: `fun.y` is deprecated. Use `fun` instead.
p

Question #3: Create a density plot.

#The Libraries are already loaded, so now for the density plot
transparentTheme(trans = .9)
featurePlot(x = data[, 1:4], 
            y = data$Species,
            plot = "density", 
            ## Pass in options to xyplot() to 
            ## make it prettier
            scales = list(x = list(relation="free"), 
                          y = list(relation="free")), 
            adjust = 1.5, 
            pch = "|", 
            layout = c(4, 1), 
            auto.key = list(columns = 3))

Question #4: Create a lineplot.

#Libraries already loaded- straight to the line plot
#I didn't even realize that I made a pun until after reviewing this
p = ggplot(data, aes(Species, Sepal.Length)) +
  stat_summary(fun.y = mean, ##adds the points
               geom = "point") +
  stat_summary(fun.y = mean, ##adds the line
               geom = "line",
               aes(group=1)) +
  stat_summary(fun.data = mean_cl_normal, ##adds the error bars
               geom = "errorbar", 
               width = .2) +
  xlab('Iris Flower Type')+
  ylab('Measurement')
## Warning: `fun.y` is deprecated. Use `fun` instead.

## Warning: `fun.y` is deprecated. Use `fun` instead.
p

Question #5: create a historgram.

#Libraries already loaded
p = ggplot(data, aes(Sepal.Width, color = Species)) + 
    geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.4) + 
    xlab("Iris Flower Type") + 
    ylab("Frequency")
p

Question #6: Create a scatterplot.

p = ggplot(data, aes(Sepal.Width, Sepal.Length)) + 
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = 'lm', color = 'black') +
  xlab('Iris Flower Types')+
  ylab('Measurements')
p
## `geom_smooth()` using formula 'y ~ x'

Correlation

Question #8: Create a Correlation Matrix.

#Libraries already all installed
cor = cor(data[,c(1:4)])
print(cor)
##              Sepal.Length Sepal.Width Petal.Length
## Sepal.Length    1.0000000  -0.1175698    0.8717538
## Sepal.Width    -0.1175698   1.0000000   -0.4284401
## Petal.Length    0.8717538  -0.4284401    1.0000000
## Petal.Width     0.8179411  -0.3661259    0.9628654
##              Petal.Width
## Sepal.Length   0.8179411
## Sepal.Width   -0.3661259
## Petal.Length   0.9628654
## Petal.Width    1.0000000

Question #9: Create a Correlation Matrix plot.

#Importing Libraries
library(corrplot)
## corrplot 0.90 loaded
#Graphing (Using the Correlation matrix from above)
corrplot::corrplot(cor)
